questions.stem: Which words were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted 'Socialist' and 'Secular' before 'Democratic Republic' and changed 'unity of the Nation' to 'unity and integrity of the Nation'. Option A is wrong because Sovereign, Democratic, and Justice were already present in the original 1950 Preamble and were not added by any amendment.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India is CORRECT?

options.option_text: The VP is elected by members of Parliament and all state legislatures
The VP acts as ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha by constitutional provision
The VP can be removed by a simple majority resolution of the Lok Sabha alone
The VP's term of office is three years and is not renewable by convention

questions.explanation: Article 64 makes the Vice President the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Option A is wrong because state legislatures play NO role in the VP election — only elected members of both Houses of Parliament vote (unlike the President's election). Option C is wrong — removal requires a resolution of Rajya Sabha agreed to by Lok Sabha, not Lok Sabha acting alone. Option D is wrong — the VP's term is 5 years under Article 67.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India.
1. The CAG is appointed by the Parliament on the recommendation of the President.
2. The CAG can be removed from office only in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
3. The CAG submits audit reports relating to the Union to the President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament.
4. The salary of the CAG is charged to the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is FALSE — the CAG is appointed by the President directly under Article 148; no Parliamentary recommendation is required. Statements 2, 3, and 4 are all correct: Article 148(1) mandates removal only through a SC-judge-equivalent address by both Houses; Article 151 routes reports through the President; and charging the CAG's salary to the Consolidated Fund insulates the office from executive budget pressure — the most PYQ-tested angle here.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
1. Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats and endow them with powers of self-government.
2. Article 44 mandates the State to implement a Uniform Civil Code within two years of the Constitution coming into force.
3. Article 39A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, provides for equal justice and free legal aid.
4. DPSPs become judicially enforceable when they relate to protection of the environment.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 40 directs organisation of village panchayats; Article 39A (42nd Amendment, 1976) provides equal justice and free legal aid. Statement 2 is FALSE — Article 44 uses the word 'endeavour' with no time limit; the two-year mandate is a fabrication. Statement 4 is FALSE — DPSPs are non-justiciable by their very constitutional character (Part IV); their subject matter, including environment, does not change this.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is CORRECT?

options.option_text: The Speaker vacates office immediately when the Lok Sabha is dissolved by the President
The Speaker can be removed by a two-thirds special majority of Lok Sabha members present
The Speaker continues in office until the newly elected Lok Sabha holds its first sitting
The Speaker votes in the first instance and uses a casting vote only in case of a tie

questions.explanation: Article 94 provides that the Speaker vacates office when the newly constituted Lok Sabha first meets — not at the moment of dissolution. This distinction is frequently tested. Option A is wrong precisely because dissolution does not end the Speaker's term. Option B is wrong — removal requires an effective majority (majority of the total strength of the House) after 14 days' advance notice, not a two-thirds special majority. Option D is wrong — the Speaker does NOT vote in the first instance; they hold only a casting vote to break a tie.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution (Anti-Defection Law).
1. A member who abstains from voting contrary to the party's direction is also liable for disqualification, not only one who votes against it.
2. The Speaker's order on disqualification is final and immune from judicial review under any circumstances.
3. A merger exemption under the Tenth Schedule is valid only if at least two-thirds of the legislative party joins the merged entity.
4. An independently elected member who joins any political party after the election is liable to be disqualified.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct. Para 2(1)(b) of the Tenth Schedule covers both voting against and abstaining from voting against the party whip (Statement 1). Para 4 disqualifies independently elected members who join any party post-election with no grace period (Statement 4). Merger exemption requires at least two-thirds of the legislative party under Para 4 of the Schedule (Statement 3). Statement 2 is FALSE — the Supreme Court in Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992) held that the Speaker's final order IS subject to judicial review; courts only refrain from intervening before the final order is passed.

questions.stem: Which of the following CORRECTLY distinguishes President's Rule (Article 356) from a National Emergency (Article 352) in terms of Parliamentary approval timelines?

options.option_text: Both require Parliamentary approval within one month of their proclamation
President's Rule lapses in two months without approval; National Emergency lapses in one month
Both require approval within two months but by different prescribed special majorities
National Emergency requires ratification by state legislatures; President's Rule does not

questions.explanation: Article 356(3) provides that President's Rule must be approved by both Houses within TWO months, otherwise it lapses. Article 352(4), as amended by the 44th Amendment (1978), reduced the approval window for a National Emergency to ONE month, with approval requiring a special majority (2/3 of members present and voting plus majority of total membership). Option A conflates the two timelines. Option C incorrectly assigns a two-month window to National Emergency. Option D is wrong — National Emergency requires no state legislature ratification; that requirement applies only to certain constitutional amendments under Article 368.
